issue.title: Launch-scratch liveness fails closed on post-birth SSH sessions, so the dead-launch backstop reclaims nothing on SSH-reached hosts

task_type_fields.impact: The sase-1bf dead-launch backstop and runner-exit cleanup silently degrade to the age-horizon fallback (`managed_tmp.horizons.build_scratch_seconds`, 1 day) on any host where the user keeps an SSH session open. apollo and athena are both reached over SSH, and their cargo-targets buckets still held 34 GiB and 70 GiB after acceptance. The refusals are visible (`dead_launch_preserved_incomplete`, runner-log `launch_scratch_cleanup` skip reasons), but not reclaimed.
task_type_fields.location: sase-core crates/sase_core/src/launch_scratch_liveness.rs (observe_unreadable / is_pre_launch fail-closed rule for unreadable post-birth processes)
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by phase bead sase-1bf.6 (host-acceptance, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #3) and triaged by the sase-1bf land agent.

On a Linux host that runs agents, open an SSH session to the host *after* a launch-keyed scratch entry (`$SASE_TMPDIR/cargo-targets/<key>` or `agent-tmp/<key>`) was created, let that launch exit (or SIGKILL it so runner-exit cleanup never ran), wait past `managed_tmp.dead_launch.grace_seconds`, and run the housekeeping `managed_tmp_reap` pass (or call `observe_launch_scratch_liveness` over the entry). The user-owned `sshd` session process is non-dumpable, so `/proc/<pid>/environ` and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` fail with EACCES for the same uid. It started after the candidate's birth time, so the sase-1bf.2 pre-launch exemption does not apply. `observe_unreadable` then marks every older candidate `complete=false`, and the dead-launch pass counts it in `dead_launch_preserved_incomplete` instead of removing it. The same rule makes runner-exit cleanup (`launch_scratch_cleanup`) skip with "liveness was incomplete" whenever an SSH login started during the agent's run and is still open at exit.

Observed during sase-1bf.6 acceptance on 2026-09-27 on apollo and athena: every production entry was preserved (explained-zero `dead_launch_removed`). Only synthetic dead keys created after the acceptance SSH session was opened were removed (`dead_launch_removed=2`). The acceptance agent's own SSH session was post-birth for every older entry.

A stale TUI's zombie children (also noted in sase-1bf.6 #3) are handled separately by the sase-1bf landing tale. This bead covers live, non-dumpable, same-uid processes that cannot have inherited the scratch environment: sshd session children, and possibly systemd --user/sd-pam restarts or tailscale SSH children. A safe rule needs design work. One candidate: a non-dumpable process whose parent chain reaches a different-uid (root) process before any same-uid ancestor cannot have inherited the launch env, because env flows parent to child only and a root parent cannot descend from the user's agent without a setuid step. Before deciding, think about sudo/setuid edge cases, including `sase sudo` and `sase_sudo_runner`.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1bf.6 host acceptance showed that the new Rust liveness observer fails closed on every live non-dumpable same-uid process that started after a scratch entry was born, most commonly an SSH session. So the dead-launch backstop removed no production entries on apollo or athena. Relaxing that rule safely needs design work beyond the epic's plan, which explicitly chose fail-closed for post-birth unreadable processes.

payload.description: Parent epic whose scratch-liveness phase (sase-1bf.2) introduced the fail-closed rule for unreadable post-birth processes; its landing tale adds the zombie exemption.
Same reaper, different blocker: sase-1bw keeps the dead-launch pass from reclaiming (liveness incomplete); this bead keeps the ordinary age pass from reclaiming (remove_dir_all fails)

evidence.note: Still live on apollo 2026-10-20 at sase 2648c7cdd and core b664b15b, after the sase-1n8 ENOSPC fixes. sase disk reap -j (dry run) preserved 267 dead-launch entries and 17 pressure candidates because 'liveness was incomplete'. The blocking processes are same-uid and non-dumpable: sshd pid 3465998 (started 13:27 UTC), gpg-agent, ssh-agent, sd-pam, npm root, and python3. New impact: the same rule defeats sase-1n8.4. Monitor-settlement reclaim skipped starter target gh_sase-org__sase-ws10-261020_091901 (created 13:19 UTC) with '3465998: environ unreadable', while targets created after 13:27 UTC were removed. It also defeats sase-1n8.5, because the emergency age only applies to complete observations. Apollo had 18 GB free and 25 GB in cargo-targets. Details: research:202610/athena_apollo_audit_triage.md.
